story_type: capsule released tumbling from a helicopter to test its parachutes
hook: A helicopter let go of this capsule and let it tumble.
narration: A helicopter let go of this capsule and let it tumble, on purpose.
SpaceX was testing the parachutes on Crew Dragon, the capsule built to carry NASA astronauts.
The tumble copied a pad abort, when a capsule blasts away from a failing rocket close to the ground.
Small drogue chutes come out first to steady the capsule. Then they pull out the big main parachutes.
[short pause] Four mains opened, low over the ground.
They carried it down toward the desert floor.
outcome: Every parachute opened, and the test backed up SpaceX's parachute models and margins.
title: Capsule dropped tumbling from a helicopter
description:
In September 2019, SpaceX dropped a Crew Dragon test capsule tumbling at low altitude to simulate a pad abort, and its parachutes deployed successfully.

Footage: NASA Kennedy Space Center video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/KSC-20190918-VP-MWC01-SPACEX-PARACHUTE

facts.source_quote: Crew Dragon parachutes successfully deploy during latest development test that simulated a pad abort, where the vehicle is tumbling at low altitude before parachute deploy, validating SpaceX’s parachute models and margins.

facts.claim: SpaceX parachute system tests took place in the western U.S. in 2019
facts.source_quote: SpaceX completed the 7th successful system test of the Crew Dragon spacecraft’s upgraded Mark 3 parachutes in the western U.S. in December 2019.
